title: Align credit memo mapping for throttled requests and billing exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We are seeing mismatches between usage-based credits created for rate-limit throttled requests (internal 'throttle credits') and the final NetSuite/Stripe export lines. Symptoms: customers report unexpected invoice subtotals where a throttle credit appears in the billing UI but is not applied to the exported invoice, or the credit is exported but not tied to the correct invoice (resulting in stale credit memos). Root causes identified in spike: 1) time-window alignment differences between the usage aggregator (UTC-day) and per-customer invoice windows (customer timezone / billing cycle boundaries) cause credit objects to be created for a different reconciliation window; 2) retries/duplicate meter events during throttle windows create offsetting usage rows that net to zero for UI but leave a positive export line; 3) rounding differences when applying per-line credits produced fractional cent deltas that NetSuite treats as separate adjustment invoices.
accepted_solution_outline: 1) Canonicalize credit generation to use invoice-anchored windows (invoice_start_timestamp) instead of aggregator-day buckets. 2) Deduplicate meter events for throttled requests at the aggregator pipeline by using idempotency keys (request_id + sequence) and emit a single credit row. 3) Emit a linking field 'credit_applies_to_invoice_id' that maps credits to the Stripe invoice id at export time; ensure NetSuite export uses that field to create a credit memo with correct parent invoice reference. 4) Apply a deterministic rounding strategy: perform subtotal rounding at invoice-level and include an explicit rounding adjustment line in exports when per-line cents mismatch exceeds 1 cent. 5) Add reconciliation checks in the export job to surface unmapped credits to the billing team for manual resolution and create automated alerts when unmapped credit ratio > 0.5% of daily credits.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All throttle-generated credits for a given billing cycle are included in the Stripe invoice payload with credit_applies_to_invoice_id populated. 2) NetSuite import creates credit memos linked to the invoice for >= 99.9% of exported credits in sanity test dataset. 3) Regression tests cover idempotent meter-ingestion for retry scenarios. 4) No customer-facing invoice subtotal differences observed for the test cohort (50 customers across timezones) during rollout window. 5) Monitoring alerts trigger when unmapped credits > 0.5%.
updates: 2025-02-12 - Triage: reported by Billing Ops after Q4 export audit. Assigned to Marcus for investigation. Added to cycle 2025-W07.

2025-02-14 - Spike: ran sample export for 2025-01 invoice window. Found 18 unmapped credits out of 3,200 exported credit rows. Observed many had event_timestamp near invoice boundary in PST vs UTC handling. Query used: SELECT invoice_id, credit_id, event_timestamp, customer_tz_offset FROM billing_credits WHERE invoice_window='2025-01' LIMIT 500;

2025-02-18 - Design decision: switch canonical window to invoice_start_timestamp. Engineering to add idempotency dedupe in aggregator. PM (Ravi Kumar) approved trade-off of adding explicit rounding adjustment lines to exports. Document uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Throttle+Credit+Reconciliation

2025-02-21 - Implementation: added credit_applies_to_invoice_id to billing schema and backfilled for Jan exports. Backfill job: gs://redwood-data/backfills/throttle-credit-link-2025-02. Job ran, fixed ~15/18 historical unmapped credits. Backfill PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/492

2025-02-25 - QA: created integration test that replays 1,000 synthetic throttle events around invoice boundaries across 6 timezones. Results: before patch exports produced 1.6% unmapped credits; after patch unmapped credits 0.04%. Test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-tests/pull/87

2025-03-01 - Code review: Runtime team reviewed aggregator changes. Feedback: ensure idempotency key uses request_id + server_sequence + model_version to avoid cross-version coalescing — updated implementation. Review link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingestion/pull/231

2025-03-02 - Rollout plan: staged deploy to billing-export-prod in 3 phases (10%, 50%, 100%) with 24h observation windows. Added export-level alert to rotate back if unmapped credits > 0.2% in any phase. Ops runbook drafted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Rollout+Throttle+Credit+Fix
testing_notes: Integration replay harness under billing-tests applies deterministic invoice ids so we can assert credit_applies_to_invoice_id equality. Added unit tests for dedupe logic (edge cases: duplicate request_id with different server_sequence) and a golden-file export for NetSuite mapping. Manual QA checklist included timezone-specific invoice generation verification for PST, CET, IST.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Backfill may create credit memos retroactively that change past accounting records; mitigation: backfill writes to a staging NetSuite export queue for manual review before final push. Risk: Slight increase in export payload size due to rounding adjustment lines; mitigation: expose combined rollups to NetSuite when small adjustments are below configurable threshold (default 1 cent).
playbook: 1) Deploy ingestion change to canary (10%) and run export pipeline against canary dataset. 2) Validate unmapped credits metric in Grafana dashboard. 3) If <0.2%, progress to 50% for 24h. 4) Run backfill in staging, review staging export report with Finance. 5) If approved, push NetSuite export for historical windows in batched groups and reconcile via automated script: scripts/reconcile_credits_to_invoices.sh. 6) Close ticket after 7-day stable observation and finance sign-off.
notes_for_support: If customers query invoice subtotals: check billing_credits table for credit_applies_to_invoice_id and whether the credit was included in the Stripe invoice payload. If credit exists but not on invoice, escalate to Billing Ops and reference backfill job ID. Use support query template: SELECT * FROM billing_credits WHERE customer_id = '{cid}' ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC LIMIT 50;
